name: timeline_super
description: Build a machine timeline with Plaso: log2timeline over an image, a partition, a directory or a collection, then psort to JSON lines (mode full), or psort alone over a storage file that already exists (mode export, for a new filter without collecting again). What the enabled parsers produced from the sources they could read, not every timestamp on the volume: a parser not enabled, a source not opened and a record not read add no row. Returns the storage file, each stage's exit code, a status (complete: both programs exited 0, wrote their files and every line parsed; partial; failed), the versions the programs print, valid and invalid line counts, first and last event, a preview sample and the log and captured-output files. complete is not coverage: the storage file's own processing report (Plaso's pinfo) says what each parser did. Slow by design; give it a narrow parser list when you know what you are after. Refuses an out_dir that already holds files unless resume is true.

out_dir.description: Where the storage file, the output, the logs and the captured output land, under work/. New or empty unless resume is true.

source.description: mode full: an image, a partition, a directory or a triage collection

mode.description: full (default: log2timeline then psort) or export (psort only, over storage_file)

storage_file.description: mode export: the existing .plaso file psort reads

parsers.description: Plaso parser filter, e.g. 'winreg,winevtx,prefetch' — far faster than the default; the installed version's help lists the names

timezone.description: The evidence machine's timezone, e.g. 'Europe/Istanbul', for the formats that store local time. Output stays UTC.

psort_filter.description: A psort event filter, e.g. "date > '2026-02-01'"; syntax is the installed psort's

sample.description: How many events to return inline as a preview (default 20)

timeout_seconds.description: One budget for every stage together, at least 30 (default 1800)

resume.description: Allow an out_dir that already holds files; only files written after this run began count as its own
